channel.title: 2026-10 on Sujith Quintelier
channel.description: Recent content in 2026-10 on Sujith Quintelier

item.title: security: Inside a malicious Claude Code-branded extension and its persistent SSH backdoor
item.description:
Microsoft describes a malicious extension branded as Claude Code that installs a persistent SSH backdoor, and provides detection and remediation guidance. The post focuses on how the extension behaves and how to identify affected systems.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Support database-level managed identity (including FIC) in Create Database Scoped Credential T-SQL
item.description:
Azure SQL Database public preview adds database-level managed identity support, including federated identity credentials (FIC), for creating database scoped credentials in T-SQL. This lets each database use a user-assigned managed identity to access Azure Blob Storage and Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 via external tables and OPENROWSET.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: security: From help desk impersonation to AD CS abuse: Investigating ESC1 and ESC8 intrusion paths
item.description:
Microsoft describes an intrusion path that began with help desk impersonation and progressed to remote access, malicious runtime execution, and abuse of Active Directory Certificate Services (AD CS). The post focuses on ESC1 and ESC8 techniques involving authentication relay and Kerberos.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Large OS Disk Encryption for Azure Confidential VM migrations
item.description:
Large OS Disk Encryption (LOSDE) is now generally available for Azure Confidential VM migration scenarios. It enables migration of larger production workloads with the OS disk fully protected.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: commandline: GitHub Universe 2026: Highlights from the developer’s developer conference
item.description:
The article says GitHub Universe 2026 centered on the developer community as the main focus of the two-day event.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: github: Webhook IP ranges added to the Meta API
item.description:
GitHub added IP ranges for webhook deliveries on github.com to the Meta API. The new ranges appear in the hooks field, so allowlists for webhook traffic should be updated from the API data.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: HTTP DDoS ruleset for Azure Front Door Premium WAF
item.description:
Microsoft announced general availability of the HTTP DDoS ruleset for Azure Web Application Firewall (WAF) on Azure Front Door Premium. The update adds HTTP-layer DDoS protection to help reduce application downtime from volumetric web attacks.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure MCP Server 3.0
item.description:
Azure MCP Server 3.0 is now generally available. The release expands Azure integration for AI agents and developer tools via the open Model Context Protocol (MCP), including new infrastructure-as-code support through Azure Terraform.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: security: IDC MarketScape names Microsoft a Leader in the 2026 Worldwide Modern Endpoint Security for Enterprises Vendor Assessment
item.description:
IDC named Microsoft a Leader in the 2026 IDC MarketScape for Worldwide Modern Endpoint Security for Enterprises.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Tracking AI adoption in North Korean threat actor tradecraft
item.description:
Microsoft Threat Intelligence reports that North Korean threat actors are increasingly using AI in their operations, with different levels of adoption across groups. The post describes how AI is being incorporated into attack chains to improve speed and efficiency.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: dotnet: Blazor Welcomes Open-Source Contributions from Syncfusion
item.description:
Microsoft and Syncfusion are collaborating on Blazor via a free open-source component toolkit, framework contributions, and developer tooling. The post says these contributions are now part of the Blazor ecosystem.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: k8s: From Working Group to SIG Architecture: spotlight on AI Conformance
item.description:
Kubernetes moved AI Conformance from a temporary Working Group into a permanent SIG Architecture subproject after establishing the initial requirements and certification process. The change is meant to keep AI infrastructure requirements vendor-neutral and aligned with Kubernetes architecture as AI workloads become more common.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: visualstudio: Preparing for Your Next Certification Could Start with Your Visual Studio Subscription
item.description:
The post says Visual Studio subscription holders may already have access to resources that can help prepare for Microsoft certification, including courses, labs, and hands-on exercises. It frames the subscription as a starting point for finding study materials and planning certification prep.

  • Source: Visual Studio Blog

item.title: commandline: Thinking about the evolution of forward-deployed engineers over the last 24 months
item.description:
The article says rapid AI model development and broader technology maturity are changing what forward-deployed engineering means. It frames the role as evolving over the last 24 months, but provides no operational details in the excerpt.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: azure: Announcing: Migrate Azure Container Apps logging destination from Log Analytics to Azure Monitor
item.description:
Azure Container Apps now treats Log Analytics as a legacy logging destination. Existing environments will keep working, but users are advised to plan migration to Azure Monitor logging.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Cross Tenant Restore with Azure Backup
item.description:
Azure Backup now supports Cross-Tenant Restore in public preview, allowing Azure VM backups to be restored into a separate Azure tenant. This provides an independent recovery path using the existing backup copy, without needing custom backup infrastructure.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: vscode: Visual Studio Code 1.144 (Insiders)
item.description:
The provided content only includes the article heading for Visual Studio Code 1.144 (Insiders) and does not contain any release details. No changelog items can be summarized from this text alone.

  • Source: VS Code Updates and Blog

item.title: ai: Introducing the Microsoft Copilot harness in Foundry Agent Service
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry is introducing the Microsoft Copilot harness in Foundry Agent Service as part of a shared execution foundation for agent experiences. It is meant to combine context, tools, execution environment, controls, and an agent loop, while preserving customer choice in supported options.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Marketplace private offer enhancements
item.description:
Microsoft Marketplace private offers now include enhancements for eligible offers, with simplified handling of pricing and terms aligned to organizational needs. The note highlights flexible billing and custom contract lengths.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Route and orchestrate models with GitHub Copilot Fusion
item.description:
GitHub Copilot Fusion is now generally available. It lets users choose Fusion instead of selecting a model per task, and Copilot will route and orchestrate which models to use automatically.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: The CISO’s evolving role: Protecting and defending in the agentic era
item.description:
Microsoft says CISOs now need to balance enabling AI/agent adoption with identity and data guardrails while also updating defenses against AI-powered threats. The post outlines how security leaders can approach both priorities in the agentic era.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot app, Universe releases
item.description:
GitHub says work often spans multiple repositories and sessions, and can also involve non-repository artifacts like specs, designs, and assets. The post announces GitHub Copilot app and Universe releases, but the provided excerpt does not include specific feature details.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Enterprise now includes access to GitHub Copilot
item.description:
GitHub Enterprise now includes GitHub Copilot for every licensed user when purchased through a GitHub or Microsoft account team. This replaces the previous model where Copilot had to be managed separately.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Security extension for the GitHub Copilot app
item.description:
A new GitHub security extension is available in public preview for the GitHub Copilot app. It lets you review and work through repository code scanning alerts without leaving the app.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub intelligence puts your code, context, and history to work
item.description:
GitHub announced “GitHub intelligence,” a set of features meant to give agents more context about how a team works, not just the codebase. The post says preferences, repository conventions, skills, and custom instructions can influence how changes are made.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Build shared workflows for your team with Copilot Automations
item.description:
GitHub is rolling out shared Copilot Automations, allowing teams to collaboratively build and maintain AI-powered workflows. The feature lets users combine prompts, triggers, and tools into team workflows.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot in VS Code, Universe releases
item.description:
GitHub says the 2026 Universe release for Copilot in VS Code adds more choice over which models you use, where agents run, and how you work with Copilot. The provided excerpt does not include the specific feature list.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Repository plugin defaults and enterprise plugin controls generally available
item.description:
Repository plugin defaults and enterprise-managed plugin controls are now generally available for VS Code, Copilot CLI, and the GitHub Copilot app. Trusted repositories can install and enable default plugins, and enterprises can manage plugin controls centrally.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Generate and edit images directly in Copilot
item.description:
GitHub Copilot now supports generating and editing images from natural language prompts. When asked for an image, the selected reasoning model uses a dedicated image-generation tool.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot Fusion now supports selection of local models
item.description:
GitHub Copilot Fusion now has experimental preview support for intelligent routing between supported on-device models and cloud models. The feature lets Fusion select local models when available.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Agentic Workflows generally available
item.description:
GitHub Agentic Workflows is now generally available. It can be used to automate reasoning-based tasks such as issue triage, CI failure analysis, and documentation updates.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: copilot-cli: 1.0.105
item.description:
Copilot CLI v1.0.105 fixes /model selection so Copilot Fusion High or Max can now be chosen from long-context sessions. This change affects model switching behavior in those sessions.

  • Source: GitHub Copilot CLI releases

item.title: vscode: VS Code Wrapped: GitHub Universe 2026
item.description:
The article says VS Code evolved from GitHub Universe 2025 to 2026, focusing on new coding workflows, collaboration with agents, and managing work across tools and environments. The provided text is a brief overview and does not include specific feature details.

  • Source: VS Code Updates and Blog

item.title: aks: Release 2026-10-25
item.description:
AKS release v20261025 adds Kubernetes 1.37 GA/LTS, makes 1.36 the default for new clusters, and ships multiple component and image upgrades. It also introduces several NAP enhancements and previews, plus notable behavior changes around automatic upgrades, Istio, AKS Automatic, etcd encryption, and VMAS-to-VMS migration.

  • Source: Release notes from AKS

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot supports server-to-server authentication
item.description:
GitHub Copilot now supports server-to-server authentication for GitHub Apps installed on organizations, in public preview. This lets services and agents built with the GitHub Copilot SDK make authenticated requests on behalf of an app without user-based auth.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Higher limit of Azure Blob Storage accounts per region per subscription
item.description:
Azure Blob Storage account quotas are now generally available at up to 1,000 standard-endpoint storage accounts per region per subscription, increased from the default 250. This allows more storage accounts to be managed within a single subscription.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Cost management and tagging for Claude models in Microsoft Foundry
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry now includes Claude model charges in Azure Cost Management with the rest of Foundry spend, and this is generally available. Previously, Claude charges were shown under SaaS instead of the Foundry resource used for deployment.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure Front Door profile and route level WAF policies
item.description:
Azure Front Door Premium now supports generally available WAF policies at the profile and route level, instead of only at individual domains. This allows broader baseline protection across an entire Front Door profile or selected routes.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: visualstudio: Visual Studio October Update – Compare Commits to Your Code, Resolve Conflicts in Bulk, Keep Coding
item.description:
Visual Studio October update adds commit-to-working-tree comparison, bulk merge conflict resolution, and several editor/UX refinements. It also refreshes Copilot chat, Hot Exit, keyboard tab controls, and Fonts and Colors.

  • Source: Visual Studio Blog

item.title: dotnet: Blazor Welcomes Open-Source Contributions from Infragistics
item.description:
Microsoft and Infragistics are collaborating on Blazor with free open-source components, new .NET 11 analyzers, and developer tooling. The post announces these contributions on the .NET Blog.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: commandline: The new primitives of agentic software delivery
item.description:
The article says agentic software delivery extends beyond code generation by connecting people, AI, and feedback across the software development lifecycle.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: k8s: Announcing the Workload Conformance Working Group
item.description:
Kubernetes announced a new Workload Conformance Working Group to define a shared, testable standard for workload behavior at runtime. The group will produce a per-minor-version specification, objective tests, and upstream conformance tooling, with initial coverage focused on runtime behavior rather than application logic.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: copilot-cli: 1.0.104
item.description:
Version 1.0.104 changes session startup and fallback behavior for Auto/Autopilot modes, updates how background-task waiting is handled, and makes Assisted Permissions available without experimental mode.

  • Source: GitHub Copilot CLI releases

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot assisted permissions generally available
item.description:
GitHub Copilot assisted permissions are now generally available in Copilot CLI, the Copilot app, and Visual Studio Code. The feature lets Copilot request permission before running commands or accessing file system paths.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GPT-6.1 Terra in GitHub Copilot
item.description:
GPT-6.1 Terra is now generally available in GitHub Copilot. GitHub says it is intended for everyday agentic coding and terminal work, and costs less than GPT-6.1 Sol.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: ai: Announcing Azure AI Speech LLM 09-2026: Broader locale support
item.description:
Azure AI Speech LLM 09-2026 adds broader locale support and claims improvements in multilingual quality and latency. The post positions the update as an expansion of supported language/locale coverage.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Network Watcher VNet flow logs filtering
item.description:
Azure Network Watcher VNet flow logs filtering is now generally available. It lets you limit logged network traffic using criteria such as IP addresses, ports, protocols, encryption state, flow state, and traffic direction.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: commandline: Cheap code, precious trust: Code modernization at scale
item.description:
The article discusses the promise and challenges of agentic software engineering for large-scale code migration and language modernization. It frames modernization at scale as a trust and execution problem, not just a tooling problem.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: visualstudio: Keep your investigation between sessions
item.description:
Visual Studio adds a standalone Markdown note for investigations and an opt-in Hot Exit preview that restores unsaved work in the next session. The post focuses on preserving work between sessions.

  • Source: Visual Studio Blog

item.title: vscode: Tune GitHub Copilot Inline Suggestions with Configurable Eagerness
item.description:
The article announces a new setting to control how proactively GitHub Copilot shows inline suggestions in VS Code. It lets users tune suggestion eagerness rather than using a fixed behavior.

  • Source: VS Code Updates and Blog

item.title: dotnet: .NET October 2026 Out-of-Band Security Updates
item.description:
Microsoft released out-of-band .NET security updates in October 2026 to address vulnerabilities in the Brotli decoder and tarball ownership handling. The post is a security notice, not a feature release.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: commandline: Building a fully autonomous meeting invite capability for Autopilot
item.description:
Microsoft describes using the Microsoft-Decision-1 model to complete an autonomous meeting-invite capability for Autopilot. The article is a brief note and provides no implementation details beyond that.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: github: Usage metrics API adds usage from tools like OpenCode
item.description:
The Copilot usage metrics API now includes model usage from additional tools, such as OpenCode, that were not previously reflected in reports.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Turn notifications into code with GitHub Copilot in Teams
item.description:
GitHub introduced a new GitHub app for Microsoft Teams that combines notifications with Copilot, letting teams act on issues and create fixes without leaving the conversation.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Item Level Recovery for Azure VMs with Premium SSDv2 and Ultra Disks in Azure Backup
item.description:
Azure Backup now supports item-level recovery for Azure VMs using Premium SSD v2 and Ultra disks, including both 512-byte and 4KB logical sector sizes. This lets you recover individual files and folders from these VMs.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: EMU deletions fix
item.description:
GitHub fixed an issue where some Enterprise Managed User accounts deprovisioned via SCIM between June 1 and June 13, 2026 were deleted instead of being suspended and obfuscated. The notice describes the incorrect deletion behavior and the correction.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: Inside the LiteLLM 1.107.0 supply chain compromise: Credential theft through Python startup hooks
item.description:
Microsoft Threat Intelligence analyzed a compromise affecting LiteLLM 1.107.0 that used Python startup hooks to steal credentials and load remote code. The post also covers detections and mitigation guidance.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: Public monitoring adds triage, validity, API, and webhooks
item.description:
Public monitoring now includes alert management features for handling leaked secrets at scale. The update adds validity checks, dismissals, timelines, filtering, plus API and webhook support.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Enterprise installations for GitHub Apps generally available
item.description:
Enterprise installations for GitHub Apps are now generally available. This lets enterprises use GitHub Apps more broadly in place of classic PATs for automation, supported by an expanded API.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot in Visual Studio — September update
item.description:
GitHub’s September 2026 Visual Studio Copilot update adds pull request exploration in chat, support for choosing the AI model your team uses, and package vulnerability fixes surfaced directly from Visual Studio.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Custom skills, agents, and MCP servers in usage metrics API
item.description:
GitHub Copilot usage metrics API now reports organization-created custom skills, agents, MCP servers, slash commands, and plugins by name instead of grouping them together.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Global default for Copilot features generally available
item.description:
GitHub is rolling out the global default policy for generally available Copilot features and supported client capabilities on Copilot Business and Copilot Enterprise. The rollout starts today and will happen gradually.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Meta API endpoints updated for Actions blob storage
item.description:
GitHub updated the meta API to include new blob storage endpoints for GitHub Actions on github.com. The change supports ongoing capacity and reliability improvements.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Public monitoring now available with data residency
item.description:
GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency now supports public monitoring in public preview. This extends secret scanning beyond internal repositories to monitor public content.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: ABFS Vectored Read for Azure Data Lake Storage
item.description:
ABFS Vectored Read is now generally available for Azure Data Lake Storage. It reduces request overhead for selective reads by batching nearby file ranges into fewer asynchronous storage requests.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Pull requests: Saved whitespace preferences and improved split view
item.description:
GitHub added two review UI changes on the pull request Files changed page: whitespace visibility preferences are now saved across pull requests, and new/deleted files have improved split-view behavior.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Industry comparisons in the Copilot impact dashboard
item.description:
The Copilot impact dashboard now adds an “Industry comparison” section. Enterprises and non-enterprise-owned organizations can compare their Copilot agentic adoption and leverage against aggregated benchmarks.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: copilot-cli: 1.0.103
item.description:
Release v1.0.103 fixes session, sandbox, and model-default handling, and improves response copying, reconnect behavior, and MCP/worktree reuse. It also updates remote launch flags and several tool-call edge cases.

  • Source: GitHub Copilot CLI releases

item.title: visualstudio: Are You Getting Everything You Can from Your Visual Studio Subscription?
item.description:
The post reminds Visual Studio subscribers that their subscription may already include benefits they can use to try Azure services, access certification learning resources, and reuse UI/dashboard components. It is framed as a prompt to explore subscription perks they may be overlooking.

  • Source: Visual Studio Blog

item.title: security: AI-driven, large-scale nation-state campaign using ARTEX enables supply chain compromise
item.description:
Microsoft says Storm-0940 used ARTEX agentic AI to speed up a ConnectWise supply-chain compromise and then abuse application credentials in Microsoft 365 environments.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: copilot-cli: 1.0.102
item.description:
Release 1.0.102 updates Copilot CLI behavior around model selection, permissions, plugin sources, shell completion, chat flow, retry handling, and sandbox networking. It also fixes a few reliability issues in subagent workflows, long-running sandboxed commands, and provider overload retries.

  • Source: GitHub Copilot CLI releases

item.title: azure: Announcing: Choose Your Own Telephony (CYOT) for Microsoft Entra
item.description:
Microsoft Entra ID will offer Choose Your Own Telephony Provider starting October 30, 2026. The feature lets organizations use a supported third-party telecom provider for SMS and voice authentication.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure Cosmos DB Safe Key Rotation
item.description:
Azure Cosmos DB Safe Key Rotation is now generally available. It adds timestamp metadata for when each account key was last used, which helps identify active keys before rotating or retiring credentials.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: vscode: Visual Studio Code 1.143 (Insiders)
item.description:
The provided content only states that VS Code Insiders 1.143 includes new features and improvements, but it does not include the actual release notes. No specific changes can be summarized from this text alone.

  • Source: VS Code Updates and Blog

item.title: github: GitHub CLI: Opt in to expiring, auto-refreshing OAuth tokens
item.description:
GitHub CLI now offers a public preview of expiring OAuth credentials that automatically refresh. When enabled, gh stores an expiring access token and uses refresh flow to keep it valid.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: visualstudio: Compare today’s code with an earlier commit
item.description:
Visual Studio now lets you compare your current working tree with an earlier commit without checking out that commit or switching branches. The feature is described in a Visual Studio Blog post about comparing historical code against today’s code.

  • Source: Visual Studio Blog

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Disable VNet peering route
item.description:
Azure announced public preview of Disable VNet Peering Route (DPR), a route-table capability that suppresses system-generated peering routes on subnets associated with the route table. This gives more control over traffic flow between peered virtual networks.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: copilot-cli: 1.0.101
item.description:
Release v1.0.101 adds several CLI and MCP workflow fixes, including native structured output for dynamic workflow subagents on supported models, new assisted approval instructions, and more reliable sign-in and permission handling. It also fixes model selection, session resume/startup behavior, Windows/macOS shell command issues, and multiple provider-specific request and image-limit problems.

  • Source: GitHub Copilot CLI releases

item.title: github: Bulk migrate branch protections to rulesets for a repository
item.description:
GitHub now lets you bulk convert all branch protection rules in a repository into rulesets in one action. This extends the existing one-at-a-time branch protection to ruleset migration.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Updates to GitHub secret scanning
item.description:
GitHub announced updates to secret scanning, including changes to audit log events and bug fixes. The notice specifically mentions a November 12, 2026 change to the business field in affected secret_scanning_alert.* and secret_scanning_push_protection.bypass audit log events.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Dependabot alerts REST API now includes dependency versions
item.description:
Dependabot alerts REST API responses now include the vulnerable dependency’s version directly. A new version_requirement field has been added to each alert’s dependency object.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Service tag match condition for Azure Front Door Premium WAF
item.description:
Service tag match conditions for Azure Front Door Premium WAF custom rules are now generally available. This lets rules match on Azure service tag IP prefix groups.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Keyless TLS on Application Gateway with Azure Key Vault Managed HSM
item.description:
Azure Application Gateway now supports keyless TLS termination with certificates stored in Azure Key Vault Managed HSM. During TLS handshakes, signatures are performed inside the HSM and the private key is not exported to the gateway.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Advanced platform metrics for Azure Monitor
item.description:
Advanced platform metrics for Azure Monitor are now generally available. The release adds finer-grained signals to help customers identify changes and trends in resources more quickly and accurately.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: GitHub package firewall in public preview
item.description:
GitHub package firewall is now in public preview. It is intended to reduce malware risks during package installation by blocking package-install-time attacks that can steal credentials from CI/CD hosts or developer workstations.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: commandline: We can build it. Can we judge it?
item.description:
The article argues that as agentic AI makes it faster to turn ideas into code, judging the resulting software becomes a more important design skill. It frames “journey evaluation” as a needed complement to rapid code generation.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: devops+ai: 🔥How AI Robot Build Institutional Knowledge Over Time🔥
item.description:
The provided content is not a release note or changelog; it is a short article title and a single phrase (“aka, write that doe Zhu Li”) with no technical update details. No actionable product changes or version information are included.

  • Source: Let’s do DevOps

item.title: github: Dependabot now supports npm 12, pnpm 11 and 12, and Bun 1.4
item.description:
Dependabot now supports upgrades to npm 12, pnpm 11 and 12, and Bun 1.4. Projects using these package manager versions can continue receiving Dependabot updates.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot model policy API for enterprise, orgs, and teams
item.description:
GitHub added REST API support to retrieve and update Copilot model policies for enterprises, enterprise teams, enterprise apps, and organizations. The change introduces new GET and PATCH endpoints for managing these policies.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot models deprecated on October 19, 2026
item.description:
GitHub deprecated a set of Copilot models on October 19, 2026 across most Copilot experiences, including Chat, inline edits, ask and agent modes, and code completions. The notice says the models are no longer available in those experiences as of that date.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Metrics usage insights for Azure Monitor workspace
item.description:
Metrics usage insights for Azure Monitor workspace is now generally available. It provides visibility into workspace metrics usage, including utilization, unused metrics, usage trends, and changes driving usage.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: copilot-cli: 1.0.100
item.description:
Release v1.0.100 adds new CLI flags and session/share commands, expands plugin and sandbox handling, and improves account, permission, and model management flows. It also fixes a wide range of reliability issues across MCP, Gemini, Windows, proxy, telemetry, and session browsing.

  • Source: GitHub Copilot CLI releases

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure DNS enables DNS-based load balancing through Traffic Manager linked records
item.description:
Azure DNS now supports DNS-based load balancing by linking a DNS record set directly to an Azure Traffic Manager profile. This removes the need to use a CNAME record pointing to Traffic Manager.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: dotnet: Get Your .NET MAUI App Ready for Xcode 27
item.description:
Microsoft published guidance for preparing existing .NET MAUI apps for Xcode 27. The post explains scene lifecycle changes and the manual migration steps needed to update apps.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: dotnet: Bring Your Own Model to the GitHub Copilot SDK with C#
item.description:
The GitHub Copilot SDK now supports BYOK, allowing apps to keep the agent runtime while routing model requests to a user-managed Microsoft Foundry or Azure OpenAI deployment. The post provides the full C# setup for this configuration.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: visualstudio: Organize and revisit tabs with the keyboard
item.description:
Visual Studio adds keyboard shortcuts to reorder document tabs and navigate back to them by their visual position. The update focuses on tab organization and quick revisiting without using the mouse.

  • Source: Visual Studio Blog

item.title: security: Agents are your newest insiders. Security must move at their speed.
item.description:
Microsoft announced new capabilities in Microsoft 365 E7 and Project Perception aimed at helping organizations contain AI agent risk and continuously adapt protection. The post frames agents as insider-like risks and focuses on security controls that keep pace with their behavior.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: Some Git over HTTPS may temporarily require authentication
item.description:
GitHub says that during periods of unusual traffic, some public repository clones and fetches over HTTPS may temporarily require authentication to protect github.com availability. The change is temporary and only affects some operations when the site is under load.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: ai: Browser automation tool in Microsoft Foundry is now GA
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry’s browser automation tool is now generally available. It adds managed browsers, native toolbox integration, Live View, and human-in-the-loop control for automating tasks on public and private websites.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: github: CodeQL changes for macOS 27, Xcode 27, and Swift 6.4
item.description:
GitHub updated CodeQL support for macOS 27, Xcode 27, and Swift 6.4 because Apple removed Intel (x86_64) code from some system binaries and libraries that CodeQL uses for build tracing. This affects how CodeQL traces builds on these platforms.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Azure Databricks Private network gateway
item.description:
Azure Databricks Private network gateway is now in Public Preview. It lets serverless compute reach resources in your VNet and transitively connected networks through a single managed gateway.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: External key management for Azure Key Vault Managed HSM
item.description:
External key management for Azure Key Vault Managed HSM is now generally available in all Azure public regions. It allows organizations with regulatory or sovereignty requirements to keep physical control of key-encryption keys while using Azure services that support this capability.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: security: Managing open-weight model risk in enterprise deployments
item.description:
Microsoft and NVIDIA released a whitepaper on managing risks from open-weight AI models in enterprise deployments. It proposes a shared taxonomy, evaluation methods, and controls for assessing and reducing those risks.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: Open source license compliance generally available
item.description:
GitHub Enterprise Cloud now generally available for open source license compliance, with ruleset-based checks to enforce centralized licensing policy across dependencies.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Xcode 27 runner image generally available
item.description:
GitHub Actions now offers the Xcode 27 runner image as generally available for building and testing Apple apps. It was previously in public preview.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Multi-repo support and other improvements for GitHub Copilot in Slack and Microsoft Teams
item.description:
GitHub Copilot in Slack and Microsoft Teams now supports multi-repository conversations, letting users work across several repos in one thread. The update also includes model and repository-related improvements.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: ai: What’s new in Microsoft Foundry | September 2026
item.description:
The September 2026 Microsoft Foundry post highlights updates across models, Routines, Tool Search, Model Router, and Insights. It presents these changes through a two-agent workflow that turns public releases into a Foundry developer changelog.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: github: Download GitHub Code Quality license usage as a CSV
item.description:
GitHub Code Quality now lets administrators download a CSV report of license usage to reconcile license counts with internal records. The report lists each active committer covered by the license usage data.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Upcoming deprecation of selected GitHub Copilot models in mid-November
item.description:
GitHub will deprecate several Copilot models on November 16, 2026. The change applies across Copilot Chat, inline edits, ask and agent modes, and code completions.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Azure Files cross-region data copy and synchronization with Azure Storage Mover
item.description:
Azure Files now supports copying and synchronizing file share data across storage accounts, Azure regions, and subscriptions within the same tenant using Azure Storage Mover. The feature is in public preview and supports scheduled incremental transfers to maintain secondary copies.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Standard service endpoint
item.description:
Azure introduced Standard service endpoint as a generally available capability in the Azure Private Link family. It is designed to provide a scalable, secure way to connect Azure IaaS workloads to Azure PaaS services, addressing manageability and scale limitations.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Availabile: Automatic zone balance for Virtual Machine Scale Sets
item.description:
Automatic zone balance for Virtual Machine Scale Sets is generally available. It continuously monitors scale sets across availability zones and redistributes VM instances when zonal imbalances are detected.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: dotnet: Introducing dotnetup: A toolchain manager for .NET
item.description:
Microsoft introduced dotnetup, a toolchain manager for .NET on macOS and Linux. It lets developers install, manage, and update user-local .NET SDKs and runtimes.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: github: AI Scan for pull requests generally available
item.description:
AI Scan for pull requests is now generally available in code scanning. It complements CodeQL by detecting vulnerabilities in pull request changes for languages and frameworks not currently covered by CodeQL.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: commandline: What will the next generation of developers do when AI writes the code?
item.description:
Microsoft and Carnegie Mellon University suggest that junior developers trained today will become the senior engineers working alongside AI-assisted coding tools in the future. The piece frames AI as part of software engineering training rather than a replacement for developers.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: visualstudio: Stop waiting on a failed build
item.description:
Visual Studio now stops solution builds after the first project failure, so you can return to fixing the error sooner. The change reduces time spent waiting for the rest of the build to finish after an error has already occurred.

  • Source: Visual Studio Blog

item.title: github: Agentic autofix for code scanning alerts general availability
item.description:
Agentic autofix for code scanning alerts is now generally available. It can investigate relevant files across a codebase and propose fixes for alerts in a developer-like workflow.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Email notifications for repository push events have been retired
item.description:
As of October 15, 2026, GitHub no longer sends email notifications for repository push events. The feature was retired to help prevent spam and abuse.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: vscode: Modernizing the VS Code UI
item.description:
The article says VS Code’s interface is being updated based on developer feedback, with changes focused on layout density, editor tabs, themes, and responsiveness. It points readers to the full post for details.

  • Source: VS Code Updates and Blog

item.title: github: HydraFusion updates and new Max option
item.description:
HydraFusion now has an updated model pool and improved orchestration workflows. A new HydraFusion Max option is also available, with both offerings supported in VS Code, the GitHub Copilot app, and GitHub Copilot.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: copilot-cli: 1.0.98
item.description:
GitHub Copilot CLI v1.0.98 adds Gemini 4 Argon support, improves command hook reliability, and fixes several session and UI/input issues.

  • Source: GitHub Copilot CLI releases

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure Cloud HSM hardware audit logging
item.description:
Azure Cloud HSM hardware audit logging is now generally available. It adds hardware-generated audit records for supported HSM management operations to aid security monitoring, compliance, governance, and forensic investigations.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure Site Recovery Support for Azure ARC-enabled Windows VMWare/Physical servers
item.description:
Azure Site Recovery now supports disaster recovery for Azure Arc-enabled Windows VMware virtual machines and on-premises physical servers. This lets customers protect Arc-managed machines with ASR while still using Azure Arc for governance and inventory.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: k8s: Why Is My Kubernetes Job Still Pending? Tracing Kueue Admission with Headlamp
item.description:
The article introduces the Headlamp Kueue plugin, which helps trace why a Kubernetes Job is still suspended by checking Kueue admission state before looking at Pod scheduling. It walks through a Headlamp-based workflow for inspecting Workloads, LocalQueues, ClusterQueues, ResourceFlavors, and Cohorts, and notes that the 0.1.0-alpha release is read-only.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: vscode: Visual Studio Code 1.142
item.description:
The provided content only states that Visual Studio Code 1.142 is available and points to the full article. No release details are included in the text supplied.

  • Source: VS Code Updates and Blog

item.title: ai: From extraction to action: Using grounding and confidence to build reliable document workflows
item.description:
The post explains how Azure Content Understanding uses grounding, field-level confidence, and calibration to support reliable document workflows. It focuses on using these signals to prioritize human review and improve extraction quality.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: visualstudio: New Tools, New Workflows and the Value of the Visual Studio Subscription: What We Learned at VSLive! San Diego
item.description:
At VSLive! San Diego, Microsoft discussed how developers are changing their coding workflows and learning new skills with Visual Studio and related tools. The post also highlights the value of a Visual Studio Subscription for expanding access to development resources.

  • Source: Visual Studio Blog

item.title: github: GitHub Actions workflow lockfiles in public preview
item.description:
GitHub Actions workflow dependency lockfiles are now in public preview for GitHub Enterprise Cloud, GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency, Team, and Free plans. They let workflows pin dependencies more reliably even if tags or branches later move.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: The hidden network: Inside the phishing infrastructure ecosystem powering global cybercrime
item.description:
Microsoft says it uncovered a Chinese-language cybercrime ecosystem linking phishing kit operators (Storm-2990) and an illicit marketplace (Storm-3119) that sold phishing tools and infrastructure. Microsoft’s Digital Crimes Unit worked with law enforcement and partners to disrupt the network.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: GitHub App improvements for least privilege and management
item.description:
GitHub released several GitHub App changes aimed at reducing reliance on classic PATs, improving app management, and helping apps request fewer sensitive permissions. The post indicates additional usability improvements for managing GitHub Apps, but the excerpt does not include the full list of changes.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: dotnet: Announcing .NET 11 Release Candidate 2
item.description:
The .NET 11 Release Candidate 2 release is available. It includes improvements across libraries, runtime, SDK, MSBuild, NuGet, F#, ASP.NET Core, .NET MAUI, and Windows Forms.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: github: Gemini 4 Argon in GitHub Copilot
item.description:
Gemini 4 Argon is now generally available in GitHub Copilot. GitHub says it is intended for complex coding, agentic, and reasoning tasks.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: copilot-cli: 1.0.97
item.description:
Release v1.0.97 adds agent-scoped declarative hooks, improves plugin/MCP handling, and fixes multiple session, permissions, and UI issues. It also changes inline images to render by default on supported terminals and includes several data/output correctness fixes.

  • Source: GitHub Copilot CLI releases

item.title: github: Audit GitHub Code Quality finding dismissals and reopenings
item.description:
GitHub audit logs now include manual dismissals and reopenings of GitHub Code Quality findings at the organization or enterprise level. This lets admins review actions on findings that appear in a repository’s default-branch backlog or other Code Quality views.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Secret scanning blocks Anthropic keys by default, adds Salesforce
item.description:
GitHub secret scanning now detects new secret types for Salesforce, Anthropic, and Cloudsmith. Anthropic keys are blocked with push protection by default.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: commandline: Copilot to autopilot: Why no single safeguard is enough
item.description:
Microsoft says it built a layered control model for an AI agent to handle production network incidents autonomously, but only within defined identity, authorization, tooling, and human-approval boundaries. The article argues that no single safeguard is sufficient for production use.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: github: Enterprise managed settings enforcement updates
item.description:
Enterprise admins can now require supported GitHub Copilot clients to fetch current server-managed settings at startup rather than using cached policy. GitHub is also adding minimum client version enforcement.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: ai: Azure Content Understanding Prebuilt Analyzers: packaging domain knowledge for document AI
item.description:
Azure Content Understanding prebuilt analyzers package domain-specific document AI logic with grounding and confidence signals. The post also shares preview benchmark results for Advanced Contextualization, including quality, modeled cost, and latency.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: github: Improved detection for withdrawn Dependabot alerts
item.description:
GitHub improved how withdrawn Dependabot alerts are identified. When an advisory or vulnerability is no longer valid, Dependabot now withdraws and removes the alert, and these changes make that state easier to detect.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Search and filter for budgets now available
item.description:
GitHub Billing’s “Budgets and alerts” page now lists all budgets in one place and adds search and filter capabilities. This makes it easier to find specific budgets in accounts with multiple entries.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Code scanning AI Scan metrics in security overview
item.description:
Organization and enterprise administrators can now view AI Scan for pull request metrics in the security overview. The new metrics track how many AI Scan findings were generated and resolved, along with related status data.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Client telemetry user attribution and configurable capture
item.description:
Enterprise administrators can now attribute GitHub Copilot activity to a user in managed settings without collecting prompts, responses, or tool content. A new telemetry.capture.identity setting provides configurable client telemetry capture options.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: dotnet: .NET and .NET Framework October 2026 servicing releases updates
item.description:
The post says it is a recap of the latest October 2026 servicing updates for .NET and .NET Framework. No specific version numbers, fixes, or release details are included in the provided text.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: github: Push attribution for commits in limited public preview
item.description:
GitHub now records the authenticated user who pushed each commit and exposes that pusher identity in the UI and API. This is in limited public preview and is available alongside the existing author and committer fields.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: dotnet: Durable Task in the Real World: What Problems Does It Actually Solve?
item.description:
The post outlines practical cases where durable execution is useful, where it is unnecessary, and how it relates to AI agents. It frames Durable Task as a tool for workflows that need reliable state, retries, and long-running coordination.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: github: Anonymous organization-level registries for Dependabot
item.description:
GitHub Dependabot now supports an Anonymous authentication method for organization-level private registries. This is intended for registries reachable without credentials, such as an internal package mirror.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: New controls and chat improvements in Copilot for JetBrains
item.description:
GitHub Copilot for JetBrains now lets users control the default model and MCP server, and includes updates that make diagnostics easier to resolve. The release also improves chat navigation and account controls.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: commandline: Introducing Microsoft-Decision-1, our model for fast decision-making
item.description:
Microsoft introduced Microsoft-Decision-1, a decision-scoring model for structured decision tasks. It is described as optimized for low latency and high quality, and positioned as outperforming both LLMs and other decision models.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot weekly releases — October 5
item.description:
GitHub Copilot’s weekly release note says this update improves cross-account and cross-environment use, while adding more control over agent access and work management. The excerpt also references GitHub Copilot Claude Haiku, but no further details are included.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: CodeQL 2.27.2 improves C++, Go, Rust, and JavaScript analysis
item.description:
CodeQL 2.27.2 is available with a new C++ regular-expression parser and analysis improvements for C++, Go, Rust, and JavaScript. The update applies to the static analysis engine used by GitHub code scanning.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: Retirement: Azure Key Vault Secrets Provider Extension for Azure Arc enabled Kubernetes clusters
item.description:
Azure Key Vault Secrets Provider Extension for Azure Arc-enabled Kubernetes will be retired on October 9, 2027. Users should migrate to the Azure Key Vault Secret Store Extension before that date.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Managed StandardV2 NAT Gateway for AKS
item.description:
AKS now provisions and manages a StandardV2 NAT Gateway for clusters using an AKS-managed virtual network. For new clusters in supported regions with managedNATGateway outbound type, StandardV2 is the default managed NAT Gateway SKU.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: security: Post-quantum authentication: Why organizations should start testing certificate ecosystems now
item.description:
Microsoft says organizations should begin testing certificate ecosystems now to prepare for post-quantum authentication. The post highlights Microsoft’s PQC TLS Pilot Program as a way to validate readiness for future post-quantum TLS deployments.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server in East US 3
item.description:
Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server is now generally available in the East US 3 Azure region. The update announces regional deployment availability.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Copilot code review: New organization billing options and controls
item.description:
GitHub added billing and license controls for Copilot code review at the organization level. Organization owners can now bill code review usage to the org for members with Copilot licenses and manage related controls.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Triage role users or higher can now archive pull requests
item.description:
GitHub now allows users with the triage role or higher to archive and unarchive pull requests. Before this change, only repository administrators could perform this action.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: Retirement: Microsoft Dev Box will be retired on September 18, 2028
item.description:
Microsoft Dev Box will be retired on September 18, 2028. The closing-down process begins on September 14, 2026, after which the service will eventually be unavailable.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Retirement: Azure Deployment Environments will be retired on February 22, 2027
item.description:
Azure Deployment Environments will retire on February 22, 2027. The closing-down process begins on September 14, 2026, after which the service will no longer be available.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Exceptions in WAF for Azure Application Gateway and Azure Front Door
item.description:
Azure Web Application Firewall exceptions are now generally available for Azure Application Gateway and Azure Front Door. The feature lets customers exclude specific parts of a request from WAF inspection to reduce false positives.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Microsoft Agent 365 integration with Azure API Management
item.description:
Microsoft Agent 365 integration with Azure API Management is now in public preview. The integration connects centralized governance with runtime enforcement for MCP servers and tools.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Screen readers can navigate timelines as lists
item.description:
GitHub issue and pull request timelines are now exposed to screen readers as lists. Assistive technology can announce the list structure, item count, and current position while users move through a timeline.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Draft pull requests count toward pull request limits
item.description:
GitHub now lets repository maintainers configure pull request limits so draft pull requests are counted too. Before this change, draft PRs were excluded from those limits.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: Announcing: Multiparty private offers in Microsoft Marketplace expands to Hong Kong
item.description:
Microsoft Marketplace multiparty private offers are now expanding to Hong Kong. This lets partners procure third-party cloud and AI solutions for customers in the Hong Kong market through Marketplace.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Claude Haiku 5.5 in GitHub Copilot
item.description:
Claude Haiku 5.5 is now generally available in GitHub Copilot. GitHub describes it as a lightweight model for fast, high-volume tasks such as subagents, quick edits, and terminal work.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: ai: Azure Document Intelligence and Azure Content Understanding: a practical guide
item.description:
The post compares Azure Document Intelligence and Azure Content Understanding, focusing on extraction architecture, workload fit, layout capabilities, deployment options, and how to evaluate which service to use. It is a practical guidance piece rather than a feature announcement.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: commandline: Bringing local models and sandboxed tools to Windows and GitHub Copilot
item.description:
GitHub Copilot is adding support for deciding when to use on-device models versus cloud models on Windows. The update also mentions sandboxed tools, but no further details are provided in the excerpt.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Anyscale on Azure
item.description:
Anyscale on Azure is now generally available. It is a managed platform for running distributed Python workloads on Ray, deployed directly on Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) and integrated with Azure services.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: vscode: Visual Studio Code 1.141
item.description:
The provided content only includes the article title for Visual Studio Code 1.141 and a prompt to read the full article. No release note details are available in the supplied text.

  • Source: VS Code Updates and Blog

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Enabling the Bulk admin role for SQL Server on Linux
item.description:
SQL Server on Linux now supports the bulkadmin fixed server role and the ADMINISTER BULK OPERATIONS permission starting with SQL Server 2025 CU9 and SQL Server 2022 CU27. This enables bulk data import operations without requiring users to be members of the sysadmin role.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Purpose-built model for leaked secret detection
item.description:
GitHub announced a new purpose-built, context-aware model for leaked secret detection as part of Secret Protection. It is intended to improve secret detection in code workflows, including those that involve AI agents.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: 3 lessons from frontier AI vulnerability research
item.description:
Microsoft Security says its FORGE Lab is applying frontier AI methods to scale vulnerability research beyond Windows, including work on the Linux kernel. The post highlights three takeaways from that research effort.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: Local sandboxing for GitHub Copilot now generally available
item.description:
Local sandboxing for GitHub Copilot is now generally available. It is supported in GitHub Copilot CLI, the GitHub Copilot app, and VS Code sessions using Agent Host.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Discover local models in GitHub Copilot CLI
item.description:
GitHub Copilot CLI version 1.0.94-0 adds a /model command so you can discover supported local models from within the CLI instead of leaving your workflow.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: devops+ai: 🔥Using Whisper, FFMPEG, and yt-dlp to Analyze Sermons for Red Flags🔥
item.description:
The article describes a toolchain using Whisper, FFmpeg, and yt-dlp to download sermon audio/video, transcribe it, and analyze the text for potentially bigoted or otherwise problematic language. It frames the approach as using AI to review sermons for “red flags.”

  • Source: Let’s do DevOps

item.title: github: Update your IDE to restore agent activity in Copilot usage metrics
item.description:
GitHub says some Copilot usage metrics showed declining agent activity and agent lines of code even as overall usage increased because of an IDE-related issue. A fix is rolling out, and users should update their IDE to restore correct agent activity reporting.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: Retirement: Pod name dimension in AKS pod platform metrics
item.description:
Azure Monitor is retiring the pod name dimension for certain AKS pod platform metrics starting September 30, 2027. These metrics will move to aggregate pod counters instead.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Stacked pull requests generally available
item.description:
GitHub stacked pull requests are now generally available. The feature lets you split large changes into smaller, focused pull requests that can be reviewed independently and merged together.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: Retirement: Azure App Service on Azure Stack Hub
item.description:
Azure App Service on Azure Stack Hub will be retired on September 30, 2029. From September 30, 2026, new installations are no longer supported and the product will receive no new releases, features, or enhancements.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Retirement: Support for Java 8, 11 and 17 will end on September 1, 2027
item.description:
Azure App Service will end support for Java 8, 11, and 17 on September 1, 2027. Apps will keep running, but security updates and customer support for those Java versions will stop.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: k8s: The Shift to cgroup v2 in Kubernetes: What You Need to Know
item.description:
Kubernetes is deprecating cgroup v1 and is moving toward cgroup v2 as the default path: in v1.35, kubelet startup fails by default on cgroup v1 nodes, and kubeadm preflight checks now error on v1.35+ when v1 is detected. The post also summarizes cgroup v2-related behaviors and features in Kubernetes 1.36, including Memory QoS, container-scoped OOM handling, PSI metrics, and in-place pod-level resource updates.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: dotnet: A faster, lighter C# Dev Kit
item.description:
C# Dev Kit has been rebuilt to open solutions in about one second and use significantly less memory. The post says it explains the changes behind those improvements.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: azure: Retirement: Always Encrypted with Intel SGX Enclaves
item.description:
Always Encrypted with Intel SGX enclaves in Azure SQL Database will retire on October 31, 2027. The retirement is tied to the phase-out of SGX-enabled DC-series hardware, and customers are directed to move to VBS enclaves.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: security: CISO perspectives on managing vulnerability risks in the age of AI
item.description:
The post says CISOs should adapt vulnerability management practices for AI-driven environments to reduce cybersecurity risk and improve resilience. It frames the topic as managing vulnerabilities in the age of AI-powered tooling and threats.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: AKS on bare metal now on Ubuntu
item.description:
Azure has a public preview for running AKS on bare metal using Ubuntu, aimed at on-premises Kubernetes deployments without a virtualization layer. The update highlights support for local control of hardware and software, with a focus on AI workloads.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: visualstudio: What Would You Build in Azure If You Didn’t Have to Ask for a Budget First?
item.description:
The post says eligible Visual Studio subscribers may already have access to a personal Azure sandbox, making it easier to try .NET apps, serverless, containers, proofs of concept, or unfamiliar Azure services without requesting a budget first.

  • Source: Visual Studio Blog

item.title: github: Code scanning AI Scan enablement status in security overview
item.description:
GitHub added AI Scan for pull requests enablement status to the security overview coverage view for organizations and enterprises. The code scanning summary now indicates which repositories have AI Scan enabled or not enabled.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Secret scanning adds detectors for Lovable, Supabase, and more
item.description:
GitHub Secret Scanning added new detectors for secrets from Lovable Labs, Pydantic Services Inc., and Supabase. A new provider also joined the secret scanning partnership program.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Azure HorizonDB expands to additional regions
item.description:
Azure HorizonDB is now available in additional Azure regions in public preview. The expansion gives users more deployment options for PostgreSQL workloads closer to applications and users.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines in Azure Bleu
item.description:
SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines is now generally available in Azure Bleu. This lets customers deploy and manage SQL Server workloads in France’s sovereign cloud while meeting data residency and sovereignty requirements.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: k8s: Scaling Kubernetes Workloads with Node Swap
item.description:
Kubernetes node swap is now GA in v1.34, and this post reports that using fast NVMe Local SSDs for swap can raise pod density for memory-heavy workloads with little latency impact when active working sets remain in RAM.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: azure: Announcing: Table discovery in OneLake Catalog search
item.description:
Starting October 15, 2026, Microsoft Fabric search will return tables from semantic models, lakehouses, and mirrored databases as separate results in OneLake Catalog search. Users will be able to find tables by name, description, or an exact column-name match.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Azure Backup for PostgreSQL flexible server and elastic cluster (v2)
item.description:
Azure Backup for PostgreSQL flexible server and elastic cluster (v2) is now in preview. It uses physical backups from managed disk snapshots and stores them in an Azure Backup vault for long-term retention.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: IPv6 Support for Application Gateway WAF
item.description:
Azure Application Gateway WAF now supports inspection and enforcement for IPv6 traffic in Public Preview. This adds IPv6 support to the web application firewall layer.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: dotnet: UWP and WinUI 3 apps: UI testing with MSTest
item.description:
Microsoft describes how to run UI tests for UWP and WinUI 3 apps using MSTest and Microsoft.Testing.Platform. It covers testing across packaged, unpackaged, and AppContainer hosts.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: commandline: Beyond violation rates: Are your AI evaluations measuring the right things?
item.description:
The article argues that structured evaluation design can make AI evaluations more comprehensive and easier to interpret. It emphasizes measuring a wider range of behaviors and producing failures that are traceable and actionable.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: commandline: Building an agentic system and a learning loop around customer IP
item.description:
Microsoft and Kantar built an agentic system around Kantar’s 30 years of ad metrics and frameworks to evaluate and help optimize advertisements. The system is described as part of a learning loop for customer IP.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: github: Stateless GitHub App installation tokens rolled out
item.description:
GitHub has completed the staged rollout of the stateless GitHub App installation token format. By default, newly minted installation tokens now use the new format.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot code review: API support and new default effort level
item.description:
GitHub Copilot code review can now be requested through both the REST and GraphQL APIs, and each request can specify an effort level. The default effort level has changed to Balanced.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Unvalidated npm trusted publishing configurations now expire
item.description:
Unvalidated npm trusted publishing configurations now expire 48 hours after creation and can no longer authorize publishing. This reduces the risk of a repository or project name changing after the configuration is created.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: npm staged publishing now supports creating new packages
item.description:
npm staged publishing now supports creating new packages. You can create a new package with npm stage publish using either a local session or a granular access token, including a stage-only token.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Selected models in GitHub Copilot deprecated
item.description:
GitHub deprecated several Copilot models across all Copilot experiences on October 2, 2026. The change applies to Copilot Chat, inline edits, ask and agent modes, and code completions.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Major version upgrades (MVU) for Azure Database for PostgreSQL elastic clusters
item.description:
Azure Database for PostgreSQL elastic clusters now support major version upgrades in public preview. Existing clusters can be upgraded in place to a newer supported PostgreSQL version without creating a replacement cluster or migrating distributed data.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: commandline: Azure Content Understanding: Building on lessons from a decade of Document Intelligence
item.description:
Microsoft reflects on a decade of document understanding work and how those lessons inform Azure Content Understanding. The piece emphasizes limits of LLMs in document reading and the importance of handling edge cases with confidence, grounding, and reasoning.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: commandline: LLM-as-translator pattern: Adding natural language understanding to an existing system without rewriting it
item.description:
The article describes using an LLM as a translation layer to add natural-language understanding to an existing system without rewriting it. The approach modernizes legacy implementations by inserting an abstraction layer instead of replacing core logic.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: github: New fields for SecurityAdvisory GraphQL API
item.description:
GitHub added five new fields to the SecurityAdvisory GraphQL object, allowing more of the GitHub Advisory Database to be read directly through GraphQL instead of using the REST API. The changelog notes one of the new fields as cveId.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Confidential comments on repository security advisories
item.description:
GitHub now supports confidential comments on repository security advisories. These comments are visible only to users with write access to the repository, allowing private discussion of a report.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Repository security advisory comments API in public preview
item.description:
GitHub has added REST API support for reading, adding, and editing comments on repository security advisories. The API also works for advisories created from private vulnerability reports.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Rate limits for private vulnerability reports
item.description:
GitHub is adding rate limits for private vulnerability reports to reduce low-quality and automated submissions that can obscure important reports. The change caps how many new reports a single account can submit.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Structured forms for private vulnerability reports
item.description:
Private vulnerability reports now support structured forms to collect the details needed for triage, including a reproducible proof of concept. This replaces reliance on a single free-text field with a more guided intake flow.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot can now interact with desktop apps with computer use
item.description:
GitHub Copilot computer use is now in public preview in Copilot CLI and the Copilot app on macOS and Windows. It can interact with desktop applications on the user’s behalf.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Actions: macOS 14 runner image retirement
item.description:
GitHub Actions will retire the macOS 14 runner image on November 2, 2026. Before removal, jobs that use macOS 14 will temporarily fail during scheduled awareness periods.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot in VS Code, September 2026 releases
item.description:
September 2026 GitHub Copilot in VS Code releases cover VS Code v1.136 through v1.140 and focus on streamlining agent-driven development from implementation through pull request merge. The update adds automations for repeatable tasks and agent merge support.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Accessibility statements highlighted on repository overview
item.description:
GitHub now highlights an ACCESSIBILITY.md file on the repository overview when it is located in the repository root, .github/, or docs/. The changelog entry also notes support for adding or proposing an accessibility statement file.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Actions retention now covers checks, runs, and statuses
item.description:
GitHub Actions retention now applies to checks, workflow runs, and statuses, using the same retention setting that already controls artifacts and logs. This means those records are now kept or removed according to the repository or organization Actions retention policy.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: aks: Release Notes 2026-09-25
item.description:
AKS release v20260925 adds GA identity bindings, preview support for Ubuntu 26.04 and Windows Server 2022 to 2025 OS SKU migration, and includes multiple behavioral changes, bug fixes, and component updates across Kubernetes versions. It also announces upcoming VMAS cluster auto-migration to VM node pools starting 2026-09-30 and notes that Windows Server 2022 is unsupported on Kubernetes 1.37+.

  • Source: Release notes from AKS

item.title: azure: Retirement: DCsv3 and DCdsv3-series Azure Virtual Machines will be retired on October 31, 2029
item.description:
DCsv3 and DCdsv3-series Azure Linux, Windows, and Dedicated Host virtual machines will be retired on October 31, 2029. After that date, they will no longer be available for use or purchase, so workloads should be migrated before then.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Scheduled code scanning skips inactive repositories
item.description:
Weekly scheduled scans for code scanning default setup and GitHub Code Quality now run only after a repository has had an analysis triggered by a push or pull request. Repositories with no recent activity no longer count toward scheduled scanning.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Code coverage uploads no longer fail CI for new branches
item.description:
GitHub Code Quality’s upload-code-coverage action no longer causes CI failures when coverage is uploaded from a branch that does not yet have an open pull request. This changes behavior from the previous failure case for new branches.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Dynamic workflows in Copilot CLI and the Copilot app
item.description:
Dynamic workflows are now available in Copilot CLI, the GitHub Copilot app, and the GitHub Copilot SDK. They let you define an orchestration in code.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: Insights from the 2026 Microsoft Digital Defense Report
item.description:
Microsoft published a brief post pointing readers to highlights from the 2026 Microsoft Digital Defense Report. The note says the security environment is becoming more interconnected, but provides no detailed findings in the excerpt.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Preparing governments for an era of interconnected cyber risk
item.description:
Microsoft says government agencies and services were the most impacted sector in 2026 cyber activity, accounting for 27% of observed activity versus 17% in 2025. The post ties this to Microsoft’s 2026 Digital Defense Report and frames it as interconnected cyber risk for governments.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog
